To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of morphological and molecular data in combination with statistical tools is a useful approach to identify pure and hybrid individuals in C. sativas and to detect the presence of different gene pools in this species.

(1) the genetic structure of the C. sativa stands analyzed was similar to that of the reference sample; (2) the genetic structure detected by STRUCTURE is consistent with the morphological classification of C. sativa individuals; and (3) the genetic structure identified within C. crenata and C. sativa was consistent with the gene pools previously detected by means of provenance tests.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of molecular and morphological data to define reference samples and to identify the genetic structure of natural populations and their hybrids, which can be useful in the management of the Castanea genus.
the development of tools for the identification of pure and hybrid Castanea species, and the identification of gene pools in natural populations.
the development of a tool for the identification and characterization of the genetic structure of C. sativa populations, and for the detection of hybrids and their genealogy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of microsatellite markers, combined with morphological traits, allows the correct classification of individuals and populations into pure and hybrid categories.
STRUCTURE is an appropriate tool to identify C. sativa pure populations, but not to identify hybrids.
C. sativa is a species that is not genetically uniform and that the two gene pools detected are not genetically uniform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of molecular markers in combination with morphological data is a useful tool for the identification of pure individuals and hybrids and for the characterization of the gene pool structure in natural populations of C. sativa.
the use of morphological and molecular tools in combination allows us to identify the pure and hybrid individuals of the C. sativa species, as well as the gene pools to which they belong.

morphological and molecular data, and the combination of both, can be used for identification of Castanea species, hybrids and their gene pools, although morphological traits may be more appropriate to identify hybrids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when the F st value is sufficiently high, the assignment of individuals to pure and hybrid populations and to their genealogical class is highly efficient, which makes it possible to use these tools to study the genetic structure of populations and to identify hybrids and their parental species.
the genetic differentiation of the Castanea species is high and that the morphological traits used in this study are not sufficient to discriminate between the Asiatic species.

the use of molecular markers, in conjunction with morphological traits and the application of statistical tools, allows the detection of hybrids and the identification of gene pools in natural C. sativa populations.
